## How I would choose between them

For your particular combination of documents, I would interview **Mitchells Solicitors, Stanford Legal and Ryder Lawyers first**, then compare their written proposals.

Here are the questions I would ask each firm\:

### Questions for your initial consultation

1. **Testamentary trust experience\:** How many testamentary trust wills do you personally draft each year, and what types of family and asset structures do you commonly advise on?
2. **Tax and asset protection\:** Can you explain the potential tax benefits and limitations, creditor risks and family-law implications of the proposed trust structure? Can you coordinate with my accountant or financial adviser?
3. **Superannuation and ownership\:** Will you review superannuation death-benefit nominations, jointly owned property, companies and existing family trusts so the plan works as a whole?
4. **Enduring power of attorney\:** Does the fee cover the EPOA, including financial and personal/health matters, and advice about who should be appointed and when their authority operates?
5. **Family circumstances\:** How would you structure the plan if there are children from previous relationships, a blended family, a beneficiary with a disability, or concerns about a beneficiary managing an inheritance?
6. **Fees and future updates\:** What is the fixed fee, including GST, for the complete package? What additional charges apply for complex trust provisions, signing, storage and later amendments?

### What should the work cost?

As one published local benchmark, Ryder Lawyers advertises estate-planning packages starting at **\$1,320 for an individual and \$1,920 for a couple**, covering a will and EPOA. More complicated arrangements may cost more, and a testamentary trust will may require a separate or higher quote. [ryderlawyers.com.au](https://ryderlawyers.com.au/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.google.com](https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id%3AChIJj70lQNBDkWsRktqoSf1sFbA&hl=en&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Don't compare quotes on price alone. Confirm whether each proposal includes the testamentary trust provisions, advice on superannuation and ownership structures, EPOAs, and any advance health directive you need.

## My bottom line

- **For specialist credentials and complex trusts\:** start with Mitchells Solicitors and ask whether Bryan Mitchell would personally handle the matter.
- **For a local western-corridor firm\:** speak with Stanford Legal.
- **For a smaller Logan-based practice\:** compare Ryder Lawyers.

One important distinction: a testamentary trust is not automatically the right choice for every estate. The best structure depends on the assets involved, beneficiaries, tax position, control arrangements and the potential cost of maintaining the trust.

**One question that would help me refine this shortlist\:** Is your estate-planning situation relatively straightforward, or do you have substantial assets, investment properties, a business or family trust, a blended family, or beneficiaries who may need asset protection? That would materially change which lawyer I would put first.

As one published local benchmark, Ryder Lawyers advertises estate-planning packages starting at **\$1,320 for an individual and \$1,920 for a couple**, covering a will and EPOA. More complicated arrangements may cost more, and a testamentary trust will may require a separate or higher quote. [ryderlawyers.com.au](https://ryderlawyers.com.au/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.google.com](https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id%3AChIJj70lQNBDkWsRktqoSf1sFbA&hl=en&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Don't compare quotes on price alone. Confirm whether each proposal includes the testamentary trust provisions, advice on superannuation and ownership structures, EPOAs, and any advance health directive you need.

## My bottom line

- **For specialist credentials and complex trusts\:** start with Mitchells Solicitors and ask whether Bryan Mitchell would personally handle the matter.
- **For a local western-corridor firm\:** speak with Stanford Legal.
- **For a smaller Logan-based practice\:** compare Ryder Lawyers.

One important distinction: a testamentary trust is not automatically the right choice for every estate. The best structure depends on the assets involved, beneficiaries, tax position, control arrangements and the potential cost of maintaining the trust.

**One question that would help me refine this shortlist\:** Is your estate-planning situation relatively straightforward, or do you have substantial assets, investment properties, a business or family trust, a blended family, or beneficiaries who may need asset protection? That would materially change which lawyer I would put first.
